name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy has been actively releasing updates through mid-2026, with the latest being v2.26.0 (July 9, 2026, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.26.0), which patches a CPU denial-of-service vulnerability in message templates and adds configurable date/time formats in the web app. v2.25.0 (June 24, 2026) introduced password reset via emailed magic links, reworked email verification to use durable single-use tokens, and replaced clock-seeded PRNGs with cryptographically secure RNG for tokens. v2.24.0 (June 4, 2026) added an opt-in in-memory ACL cache (`auth-access-cache`) to reduce database load and fixed a critical case-insensitive ACL topic matching bug on SQLite. Earlier releases (v2.23.0) added per-visitor topic creation rate limits and fixed a same-origin script execution vulnerability in the publish dialog.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL 2.0 (client), per project documentation
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026 with active community contributions
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — user accounts, access tokens, ACL with per-topic rules, and auth-default-access policies
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted instance

breaking_excerpts: v2.24.0: Fixed case-insensitive ACL topic matching on SQLite — access control rules for 'secret' no longer match 'SECRET'; behavior change for existing SQLite-based deployments with mixed-case topic rules.
v2.25.0: Email verification reworked from in-memory 6-digit codes to durable magic links; existing unverified email flows are replaced.
v2.25.0: X-Email: yes now requires being logged in with a verified primary address, regardless of smtp-sender-verify setting — previously worked without verification enabled.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a versatile notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server like ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notifications and file sharing but is closed-source, has a limited free tier, and is not self-hostable.

alternatives.name: Ntopng / Alertmanager (Prometheus)
alternatives.review: Alertmanager is powerful for infrastructure alerting with routing and grouping but is narrowly focused on metrics-based alerts rather than general-purpose push notifications.
